title: College Physics 2e
creator: OpenStax, Rice University
prerequisites: Algebra and some trigonometry; no calculus.
access: Free web and PDF; paid print editions.
why: A broad reference when a project exposes a gap in forces, energy, waves or electricity.
first_task: Work a units and force problem, then annotate the assumptions in your own bracket load sketch.
limitations: A substantial textbook; select relevant sections rather than delaying all projects until you finish it.
evidence_note: Official preface confirms algebra-based scope, no calculus prerequisite, practice problems and free web/PDF access.

title: Precalculus 2e
creator: OpenStax, Rice University
prerequisites: Comfort with fractions, signed numbers, and elementary algebra, including linear equations and powers; review these first if rusty.
access: Free web and PDF; paid print editions.
why: A structured bridge for functions, angles and trigonometry used in CAD and robotics.
first_task: Use the angles and unit-circle section to calculate the endpoint of a 60 mm arm at two angles.
limitations: Longer than a quick refresher; use your failed calculation to choose a section.
evidence_note: Official preface confirms functions and trigonometry coverage, worked examples and access formats.

title: Vectors, what even are they? / Essence of linear algebra
creator: Grant Sanderson, 3Blue1Brown
access: Free official lesson with video and text adaptation.
why: Useful visual intuition for relating arrows to ordered components before coordinate transforms.
first_task: Pause at a vector addition example and draw the result before continuing.
limitations: Visual understanding needs worked exercises; this lesson does not teach robot mechanics or control.
evidence_note: Official lesson confirms author, vector interpretations, coordinates and operations; linked series continues linear algebra.

title: Single Variable Calculus, 18.01SC (Fall 2010)
creator: MIT OpenCourseWare, David Jerison and course team
access: Free archived course materials, videos and solutions; no enrolled instruction or certificate included.
why: A complete independent-study route when rates, accumulation and optimization become recurring project needs.
first_task: Complete the first differentiation worked examples and solve a problem before viewing its solution.
limitations: Archived course; old Java applets may not run in modern browsers. Core readings, videos and exercises remain the intended route.
evidence_note: Official page lists lectures, recitations, worked examples, problem sets, exams and solutions, and explicitly describes independent-study design.

title: Guidelines for Evaluating and Expressing the Uncertainty of NIST Measurement Results, TN 1297
creator: Barry N. Taylor and Chris E. Kuyatt, NIST
prerequisites: Means, standard deviation, units and a clearly defined measurement.
access: Free official web text and PDF.
why: A precise next step after simple repeatability experiments, especially for separating uncertainty contributions.
first_task: List Type A and Type B evaluation inputs for one measurement without relabeling them random and systematic.
limitations: Formal metrology guidance, not a beginner caliper tutorial; a defensible budget requires a suitable measurement model.
evidence_note: Official index confirms 1994 edition, authors and sections on Type A/B, combination, expanded uncertainty and reporting.

title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook: Choosing an experimental design
creator: NIST/SEMATECH
prerequisites: Basic statistics and a measurable response.
why: Helps move beyond ad hoc comparisons when several process factors and interactions matter.
first_task: Define two factors and two levels for a harmless placement experiment, then identify what could confound the comparison.
limitations: Requires study of assumptions; a factorial table alone does not validate a process or establish safety.
evidence_note: Official section lists objectives, variables, randomized and block designs, full/fractional factorial designs and confounding.

title: Design Thinking Bootleg (2018)
creator: Stanford d.school
prerequisites: A real task to observe and a willingness to revise assumptions.
access: Free downloadable method cards; separate from university enrollment.
why: A practical source of observation and prototyping methods when you are unsure what question to ask next.
first_task: Choose one observation method and turn a witnessed difficulty into a testable need.
limitations: Methods support inquiry; they do not supply engineering calculations or prove a product will succeed.
evidence_note: Official page confirms downloadable cards, five modes, 2018 credits and the method-based format.

title: The Design of Everyday Things, Revised and Expanded Edition
creator: Don Norman; Basic Books
prerequisites: No engineering prerequisite; observe ordinary products while reading.
access: Paid print, ebook and audio formats; library availability varies.
why: Builds a vocabulary for visible controls, feedback and understandable interaction.
first_task: Analyze one confusing adjustment or fastening action, then sketch a change and test it without coaching.
limitations: Human-centered design foundation; it does not replace mechanical, electrical or manufacturing validation.
evidence_note: Publisher confirms revised edition, author, formats and human-centered design scope. No current stock or price claim.

title: Product Design and Development, 15.783J (Spring 2006)
creator: MIT OpenCourseWare; Kressy, Eppinger, Roemer and Seering
prerequisites: A small project; willingness to combine user needs, concepts and manufacturing constraints.
access: Free archived notes and assignments; assigned commercial books/cases may require separate access.
why: A deeper framework for coordinating design decisions across a complete project.
first_task: Use the customer-needs and concept work to compare three genuinely different bracket concepts.
limitations: Graduate course archive, not a complete video course or current live class; feedback and team experience must be arranged separately.
evidence_note: Official course and syllabus confirm graduate 2006 offering, notes, assignments, examples and integration of design/manufacturing/marketing.

title: Fab Academy program and public project archives
creator: Fab Academy
level: Intermediate; beginner route requires substantial time
prerequisites: Access to suitable supervised fabrication resources for enrolled hands-on work.
access: Public archives and linked class videos; enrolled program and lab participation have tuition and local access requirements.
why: Useful as an integrated project-learning model and a source of documented iteration examples.
first_task: Read one complete student project record and identify its interface tests, failed attempts and revision evidence.
limitations: Reading public material is not enrollment, assessment or permission to operate a machine; schedules and local fees vary.
evidence_note: Official page confirms multidisciplinary hands-on program, local nodes, documentation, archive/video links and tuition navigation.
